r1-observability-1.summary: Notification-service is experiencing delayed processing due to slow external vendor calls (sms-vendor and push-provider) starting around 14:02, which correlates with an increasing consumer lag on the event-bus starting at 14:07.

findings.statement: Metrics queries for notification-service failed with a 503 Service Unavailable error.
Event-bus consumer_lag metric showed an upward anomaly starting at 2026-10-12T14:07:00+00:00, peaking at 1006.69 messages at 14:33:00+00:00.
Event-bus request rate, error rate, p99 latency, and CPU usage remained stable and showed no anomalies.
Notification-service logged slow outbound requests to sms-vendor starting at 2026-10-12T14:02:53+00:00.
Notification-service logged slow outbound requests to push-provider starting at 2026-10-12T14:06:19+00:00.
Notification-service logged consumer group notif-alerts lag warnings starting at 2026-10-12T14:18:26+00:00.

open_questions: What caused sms-vendor and push-provider response times to degrade?
Why did notification-service internal metrics fail with 503 errors?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped service dependencies around notification-service, event-bus, sms-vendor, and push-provider, and reviewed all deployment, configuration, and feature flag changes across the platform over the past 7 days.

findings.statement: notification-service consumes messages asynchronously from event-bus and makes synchronous calls to sms-vendor and push-provider.
payments-api produces messages asynchronously to event-bus.
notification-service underwent a scheduled API credentials rotation (chg-9140) at 2026-10-12T07:38:00+00:00, prior to the reported symptom onset around 14:00.
event-bus had its request timeout raised from 5s to 6s (chg-8599) at 2026-10-12T05:21:00+00:00.

open_questions: Whether the credential rotation on notification-service or any downstream vendor throttling contributed to the SMS and push notification delivery delays.

r2-observability-1.summary: sms-vendor experienced latency spikes starting around 14:05, confirming external vendor performance degradation that aligns with the delayed transaction alerts.

findings.statement: sms-vendor latency_p99_ms experienced an anomaly starting at 2026-10-12T14:05:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 1569.0 ms at that time.

hypotheses.title: External Vendor Latency Degradation in SMS and Push Providers
hypotheses.mechanism: sms-vendor and push-provider experienced internal latency spikes (verified via sms-vendor p99 latency anomaly at 14:05 and notification-service outbound call warnings at 14:02 and 14:06). Because notification-service makes synchronous calls to these vendors, these slow responses caused worker threads to block, backing up asynchronous message consumption from event-bus and resulting in consumer lag starting at 14:07.

supporting.note: Shows outbound requests to sms-vendor taking over 5.5 seconds starting at 14:02.
Confirms sms-vendor p99 latency anomaly starting at 14:05, peaking at 1569.0 ms.
Shows outbound requests to push-provider taking over 7.2 seconds starting at 14:06.
Shows consumer lag increasing sharply starting at 14:07, peaking at over 1000 messages.
Confirms warning logs for consumer group notif-alerts lag starting at 14:18.
Past incident shares exact symptom and root-cause category of sms-vendor delays.

contradicting.note: sms-vendor error rate showed no anomalous behavior during the window.
sms-vendor request rate remained stable with no traffic surge.

assumptions: sms-vendor and push-provider suffered internal capacity or routing degradation outside of our platform control.

hypotheses.title: Notification-Service Internal Resource Bottleneck
hypotheses.mechanism: notification-service experienced internal resource exhaustion, causing its metrics backend to fail with 503 errors and leading to slow outbound calls to vendors as well as event-bus consumer lag.

contradicting.note: sms-vendor experienced its own p99 latency anomaly starting at 14:05, indicating the bottleneck was vendor-side.
Outbound call logs show vendor-side latency rather than client-side connection exhaustion.

assumptions: The 503 errors when querying notification-service metrics are due to an internal service crash or resource exhaustion rather than a monitoring/telemetry backend failure.

hypotheses.title: Notification-Service Credential Rotation Side-Effect
hypotheses.mechanism: The scheduled API credential rotation on notification-service at 07:38 introduced latent client-side delays or authentication overhead that manifested as slow outbound requests to vendors several hours later.

supporting.note: A config change (credentials rotation) was executed on notification-service earlier in the day at 07:38.

contradicting.note: The time gap between the change at 07:38 and the symptom onset at 14:02 is over 6 hours, with successful operation in between.
notification-service successfully processed payment intents and other requests normally hours after the change.

assumptions: A credential rotation can cause clean operation for over 6 hours before manifesting as severe latency on vendor calls.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: Addressing the Critic's points: We successfully retrieved sms-vendor telemetry (metric:sms-vendor:latency_p99_ms), confirming a p99 latency anomaly starting at 14:05 peaking at 1569.0 ms, directly supporting H1. Regarding notification-service metrics failing with 503 errors, direct internal resource metrics remain unavailable, but indirect evidence (outbound vendor latency logs starting at 14:02 and 14:06, and subsequent event-bus consumer lag from 14:07) robustly points to external vendor latency as the root cause rather than an internal service failure. Past incident hist-2026-0325 shares the exact symptom and root-cause category ('Transaction SMS delayed' due to sms-vendor). H1 remains our best-supported hypothesis (confidence 0.82), with H2 and H3 retained as weaker alternatives.
